findings.claim: The supplied router implements six horizontal foundation procedures: identity.session, identity.scopes, identity.entry, identity.createInitialBond, identity.syncCredentials and authority.refreshSnapshot. The catalog admits all six for the app channel with session assurance and required G2 evidence; it classifies createInitialBond and refreshSnapshot as commands and the others as queries.

Every supplied router handler is behind a shared identity-and-platform presence guard. syncCredentials reports SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE when its issuer is missing. These visible guards do not establish the correctness of authentication, delegated security checks, deployed execution or G2 verification.

The feature description's unqualified statement that the reset v1 contract is empty is superseded as a description of the entire current API by the six implemented and admitted foundation procedures. Its narrower empty-business-contract language remains consistent with the supplied router, which contains only identity and authority namespaces. This is an evolution of foundation implementation, not evidence of business admission.

The governing policy still authorizes horizontal foundation work and expressly defers business admission, feature migrations and unresolved product policies. Its implementation snapshot claiming two read-only identity procedures is stale against the supplied router and catalog; that stale snapshot does not invalidate the continuing scope restriction.

The existing intent is to establish authorized, durable horizontal operations before product capabilities, preserve canonical account identity and existing authority, and demonstrate reliability through isolated PostgreSQL and synthetic capabilities. The journey labels implementation implemented and verification partial; those labels are recorded intent/status, not independently observed test evidence.

Neither admission of the six foundation procedures nor their G2 requirement authorizes implementing business procedures. The supplied catalog itself leaves owner confirmation of the G2 admission bar pending, and a required evidence level does not prove that evidence exists or passes.
